q1.text: What does a red octagonal sign mean?
q1.explain: A red octagonal sign is a STOP sign. You must come to a complete stop.

q2.text: What is the speed limit in residential areas in Saudi Arabia?
q2.explain: The speed limit in residential areas is typically 40 km/h unless otherwise posted.

q3.text: When should you use your vehicle's headlights?
q3.b: During rain, fog, or low visibility
q3.explain: Use headlights during rain, fog, sandstorms, or any condition with reduced visibility.

q4.text: What does a flashing yellow traffic light mean?
q4.explain: A flashing yellow light means proceed with caution. Slow down and be prepared to stop.

q5.text: What do double solid yellow lines in the center of the road indicate?
q5.explain: Double solid yellow lines mean no passing is allowed from either direction.

q6.text: What is the maximum speed limit on highways in Saudi Arabia?
q6.explain: The maximum speed limit on highways in Saudi Arabia is typically 120 km/h for cars.

q7.text: Who is required to wear a seatbelt in Saudi Arabia?
q7.explain: All occupants of a vehicle are required to wear seatbelts in Saudi Arabia.

q8.text: What does a triangular sign with the point facing down mean?
q8.explain: An inverted triangle (point down) is a yield/give way sign. You must give priority to other traffic.

q9.text: At a roundabout, who has the right of way?
q9.d: Vehicles coming from the right only
q9.explain: Vehicles already circulating in the roundabout have the right of way.

q10.text: What is the safe following distance rule?
q10.explain: Maintain a 2-3 second gap from the vehicle ahead. Increase this in bad weather.

q11.text: What must you do when a traffic light turns red?
q11.b: Slow down but proceed if clear
q11.explain: You must come to a complete stop before the stop line when the traffic light is red.

q12.text: What does a red circle with a white horizontal bar mean?
q12.explain: A red circle with a white horizontal bar is the 'No Entry' sign. Vehicles cannot enter.

q13.a: On straight roads with good visibility
q13.b: Near curves, hills, intersections, and pedestrian crossings
q13.explain: Overtaking is prohibited near curves, hills, intersections, pedestrian crossings, and where marked.

q14.text: What should you do when an emergency vehicle approaches with sirens?
q14.a: Speed up to get out of the way
q14.c: Pull over to the right and stop
q14.explain: Pull over to the right side of the road and stop to allow emergency vehicles to pass.

q15.text: What do white zebra stripes on the road indicate?
q15.explain: White zebra stripes indicate a pedestrian crossing. Drivers must yield to pedestrians.

q16.text: How far from a fire hydrant must you park?
q16.explain: You must park at least 5 meters away from a fire hydrant to allow emergency access.

q17.text: What does it mean when a traffic police officer extends their arm horizontally?
q17.a: Stop for vehicles approaching from that direction
q17.explain: An extended arm means stop for vehicles approaching from that direction.

q18.text: What should you do if your tire blows out while driving?
q18.b: Grip the steering firmly, ease off the gas, and slow down gradually
q18.c: Turn sharply to the side of the road
q18.explain: Hold the steering wheel firmly, gradually ease off the accelerator, and slow down safely.

q19.text: A circular sign with a red border and black number '60' means:
q19.explain: A red-bordered circular sign with a number indicates the maximum speed limit.

q20.text: Is using a mobile phone while driving allowed in Saudi Arabia?
q20.explain: Using a handheld mobile phone while driving is strictly prohibited in Saudi Arabia.

q21.text: How do wet roads affect braking distance?
q21.c: Braking distance can double or more
q21.explain: Wet roads reduce tire traction, which can double or triple your braking distance.

q22.text: What does a blue circular sign with white arrows in a circle mean?
q22.explain: A blue circular sign with white circular arrows indicates a roundabout ahead.

q23.text: What do white arrows painted on the road indicate?
q23.b: Direction you must travel in that lane
q23.explain: Road arrows indicate the permitted direction(s) of travel for that lane.

q24.text: What is the minimum age to obtain a driving license in Saudi Arabia?
q24.explain: You must be at least 18 years old to obtain a private driving license in Saudi Arabia.

q25.text: What does a green arrow signal at a traffic light mean?
q25.c: You may proceed in the direction of the arrow
q25.explain: A green arrow allows you to proceed safely in the direction the arrow points.

q26.text: Where should children under 10 years old sit in a vehicle?
q26.explain: Children under 10 must sit in the back seat with appropriate child restraints.

q27.text: A yellow diamond sign with a curved arrow indicates:
q27.explain: Yellow diamond signs are warning signs. A curved arrow warns of a curve ahead.

q28.text: When parking uphill with a curb, which way should your front wheels point?
q28.explain: When parking uphill with a curb, turn wheels away from curb so the car rolls into the curb if brakes fail.

q29.text: What is the best action if you feel drowsy while driving?
q29.explain: If drowsy, the only safe action is to pull over and rest. Temporary fixes don't work.

q30.text: When should you use hazard warning lights?
q30.b: When your vehicle has broken down or is stationary and causing an obstruction
q30.explain: Use hazard lights when your vehicle is broken down, in an emergency, or obstructing traffic.

q31.text: What does a circular sign with a red border, blue background, and red diagonal line mean?
q31.explain: A blue circle with red border and single diagonal line means no parking.

q32.text: On a multi-lane road, which lane is for overtaking?
q32.explain: In Saudi Arabia, the left lane is for overtaking. Return to the right after passing.

q33.a: An area where your vision is blocked by the sun
q33.b: An area not visible in your mirrors that requires a head check
q33.explain: A blind spot is an area around your vehicle not visible in mirrors. Always check by turning your head.

q34.text: What does 'BUS' written in a lane indicate?
q34.explain: BUS marked on a lane means it is reserved for buses only during operating hours.

q35.text: What is the typical speed limit in school zones when children are present?
q35.explain: School zones typically have a 30 km/h speed limit when children are present.

q36.text: When is it appropriate to use your horn?
q36.b: To warn others of danger or your presence
q36.d: Late at night in residential areas
q36.explain: Use your horn only to warn other road users of danger or to make your presence known.

q37.text: What should you do at a railway crossing when the barrier is down?
q37.a: Go around the barrier if no train is visible
q37.b: Wait until the barrier is fully raised
q37.c: Proceed slowly if the train has passed
q37.explain: Always wait until the barrier is fully raised before proceeding at a railway crossing.

q38.text: What does a blue square sign with a white walking figure indicate?
q38.explain: Blue signs with pedestrian symbols indicate pedestrian crossings or zones.

q39.text: What is the legal blood alcohol limit for driving in Saudi Arabia?
q39.explain: Alcohol is completely prohibited in Saudi Arabia. There is zero tolerance for driving under the influence.

q40.text: What is the primary purpose of an airbag?
q40.b: To cushion occupants during a collision
q40.d: To make the car look modern
q40.explain: Airbags cushion occupants and reduce impact forces during a collision. They work with seatbelts, not as replacements.

q41.text: What does a broken white line in the center of the road mean?
q41.explain: A broken white line indicates you may cross it to overtake when it is safe to do so.

q42.text: When should you use fog lights?
q42.b: Only in heavy fog or severely reduced visibility
q42.explain: Use fog lights only in conditions of heavy fog, mist, or when visibility is seriously reduced.

q43.text: What does a blue rectangular sign with a white arrow pointing up mean?
q43.explain: A blue rectangular sign with a white arrow pointing ahead indicates a one-way street.

q44.b: When tires lose contact with the road due to water
q44.explain: Aquaplaning occurs when tires ride on top of water, losing contact with the road surface.

q45.text: Who has priority at a zebra crossing?
q45.explain: Pedestrians have priority at zebra crossings. Drivers must stop to let them cross.

q46.text: How far before turning should you signal?
q46.explain: Signal at least 30 meters before turning to give other road users adequate warning.

q47.text: When driving at night, what should you do when another vehicle approaches with high beams on?
q47.b: Look at the right edge of the road
q47.explain: Look toward the right edge of the road to avoid being blinded by oncoming high beams.

q48.text: What does a sign with black diagonal stripes on white background mean?
q48.explain: Black diagonal stripes on white indicate the end of all previously applicable restrictions.

q49.text: What must you do when entering a tunnel?
q49.a: Turn on headlights and remove sunglasses
q49.explain: Always turn on headlights when entering a tunnel and remove sunglasses to adjust to the lower light.

q50.text: How often should you check your tire pressure?
q50.b: At least once a month and before long trips
q50.explain: Check tire pressure at least monthly and before any long journey for safety and fuel efficiency.

vp-001.text: According to traffic regulations, how many violation points can lead to license suspension within a Hijri year?
vp-001.explain: In general practice, accumulating 24 violation points can lead to suspension.

vp-002.text: What happens the first time a driver reaches 24 violation points within a Hijri year?
vp-002.explain: First time reaching 24 violation points results in a 3-month suspension.

vp-003.text: What is the penalty the second time a driver reaches 24 violation points within a Hijri year?
vp-003.explain: Second time reaching 24 violation points results in a 6-month suspension.

vp-004.text: What is the penalty the third time a driver reaches 24 violation points within a Hijri year?
vp-004.explain: Third time reaching 24 violation points results in a 1-year suspension.

vp-005.text: What happens the fourth time a driver reaches 24 violation points within a Hijri year?
vp-005.explain: Fourth time reaching 24 violation points leads to permanent revocation.

vp-006.text: In general practice, the 24-violation-point limit is calculated within which period?
vp-006.explain: The 24-violation-point limit is calculated within a Hijri year.

vp-007.text: How many violation points are assigned for driving a vehicle under the influence (Alcohol/Drugs)?
vp-007.explain: Driving under the influence carries 24 violation points.

vp-008.text: How many violation points are assigned for drifting?

vp-009.text: How many violation points are assigned for running a red traffic light?
vp-009.explain: Running a red light carries 12 violation points.

vp-010.text: How many violation points are assigned for driving in the opposite direction of traffic?
vp-010.explain: Driving in the opposite direction carries 12 violation points.

vp-011.text: How many violation points are assigned for weaving through traffic on public roads?
vp-011.explain: Weaving through traffic carries 8 violation points.

vp-012.text: How many violation points are assigned for not complying with a traffic officer’s manual signal?
vp-012.explain: Not complying with the officer’s signal carries 8 violation points.

vp-013.text: How many violation points are assigned for driving a vehicle without brakes or lights?
vp-013.explain: Driving without brakes or lights carries 8 violation points.

vp-014.text: How many violation points are assigned for not stopping completely at a stop sign?
vp-014.explain: Not stopping at a stop sign carries 6 violation points.

vp-015.text: Failing to observe right-of-way rules results in how many violation points?
vp-015.explain: Failing to observe right-of-way carries 6 violation points.

vp-016.text: Exceeding the speed limit by more than 25 km/h results in how many violation points?
vp-016.explain: Speeding more than 25 km/h carries 6 violation points.

vp-017.text: Not yielding to cars inside a roundabout results in how many violation points?
vp-017.explain: Not yielding in roundabouts carries 6 violation points.

vp-018.text: Overtaking in prohibited areas results in how many violation points?
vp-018.explain: Overtaking in prohibited areas carries 6 violation points.

vp-019.text: Stopping on railway tracks results in how many violation points?
vp-019.explain: Stopping on railway tracks carries 6 violation points.

vp-020.text: Exceeding the speed limit by up to 25 km/h results in how many violation points?
vp-020.explain: Speeding up to 25 km/h carries 4 violation points.

vp-021.text: Driving on lanes not designated for the vehicle results in how many violation points?
vp-021.explain: Driving on non-designated lanes carries 4 violation points.

vp-022.text: Overtaking school buses while students are boarding or disembarking results in how many violation points?
vp-022.explain: Overtaking school buses carries 4 violation points.

vp-023.text: Not covering the load and cargo during transport results in how many violation points?

vp-024.text: Modifying vehicle structure or body without proper authorization results in how many violation points?

vp-025.text: Not wearing a seatbelt results in how many violation points?
vp-025.explain: Not wearing a seatbelt carries 2 violation points.

vp-026.text: Using a hand-held mobile phone while driving results in how many violation points?
vp-026.explain: Using a hand-held mobile phone carries 2 violation points.

vp-027.text: Not wearing a helmet while riding motorized bikes results in how many violation points?
vp-027.explain: Not wearing a helmet carries 2 violation points.

tf-001.text: In general practice, what is the main purpose of traffic fines?
tf-001.a: To improve road safety and reduce accidents
tf-001.explain: Fines are intended to encourage safer driving habits.

tf-002.text: Which type of violation usually carries the highest fine?
tf-002.a: Very serious violations that endanger lives
tf-002.explain: Very serious violations typically carry the highest fines.

tf-003.text: Why can fines increase for repeated violations?
tf-003.explain: Repeat violations usually lead to higher penalties to encourage compliance.

tf-004.text: Are traffic fines intended to improve road safety?
tf-004.b: No, they are only for revenue
tf-004.explain: Fines are designed to promote safer driving.

tf-005.text: Minor traffic violations usually result in:
tf-005.explain: Minor violations generally carry lower fines.

tf-006.text: In practice, not wearing a seatbelt usually results in:
tf-006.explain: Seatbelt violations are typically treated as moderate.

tf-007.text: Using a hand-held mobile phone while driving usually results in:
tf-007.explain: Phone use while driving is treated as more serious.

tf-008.text: Serious violations like running a red light are usually punished with:
tf-008.explain: Dangerous behavior usually carries higher fines.

tf-009.text: Light speeding is generally categorized as:
tf-009.explain: Light speeding is typically treated as moderate.

tf-010.explain: Parking issues are usually categorized as minor.

tf-011.a: A serious violation with higher fines
tf-011.explain: Excessive speeding is treated as serious.

tf-012.text: Very serious violations usually lead to:
tf-012.explain: Very serious violations can carry heavier fines and penalties.

hb-001.text: What is the minimum age to get a Private-car driving license?
hb-001.explain: The minimum age for a private car license is 18 years.

hb-002.text: How long is a private driving license valid?
hb-002.explain: A private driving license is valid for 10 years.

hb-003.text: How long is a public driving license valid?
hb-003.explain: Public driving licenses are valid for 5 years.

hb-004.text: What is the minimum age to drive a motorcycle?
hb-004.explain: The minimum age for riding a motorcycle is 18 years.

hb-005.text: What is the stopping distance at 50 km/h on a dry road?
hb-005.explain: At 50 km/h: reaction distance is 15m + braking distance is 25m = stopping distance of 40m.

hb-006.text: What is the stopping distance at 100 km/h on a dry road?
hb-006.explain: At 100 km/h: reaction distance 30m + braking distance 100m = 130m stopping distance.

hb-007.text: What is the reaction time assumed in the standard stopping distance formula?
hb-007.explain: Standard reaction time is assumed to be 1 second in stopping distance calculations.

hb-008.text: When does the reaction distance become longer?
hb-008.explain: Reaction distance increases at high speeds, if you are distracted or tired, or under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

hb-009.text: What number do you call for the Red Crescent in an accident with injuries?
hb-009.explain: Call the Red Crescent at 997 for accidents with injuries.

hb-010.text: What is the maximum damage amount for an accident to be classified as 'minor'?
hb-010.explain: A minor accident involves property damage not exceeding 5,000 SAR and injuries not requiring hospitalization.

hb-011.text: How many points result in the withdrawal of a driver's license?
hb-011.explain: The driver's license is withdrawn when the total number of points reaches 24.

hb-012.text: How many points are assigned for driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs?
hb-012.explain: Driving under the influence carries the maximum penalty of 24 points.

hb-013.text: How many points are assigned for running a red light?
hb-013.explain: Not stopping while a red light is on carries 12 points.

hb-014.text: How many points for not wearing a seat belt?
hb-014.explain: Not wearing a seat belt carries 2 points.

hb-015.text: What is the fine for drifting on the FIRST offense?
hb-015.explain: The first drifting offense: vehicle impounded 15 days + 20,000 SAR fine + possible imprisonment.

hb-016.text: What happens on the THIRD drifting offense?
hb-016.explain: Third drifting offense results in confiscation of the vehicle and a 60,000 SAR fine.

hb-017.text: How many days does the driver have to pay the minimum fine before the maximum is imposed?
hb-017.explain: The violating driver may pay the minimum fine within a maximum period of 30 days from the date of the violation.

hb-018.text: How long is the license withdrawn for the FIRST time the point limit is reached in one Hijri year?
hb-018.explain: For the first time in one Hijri year, the driver's license is withdrawn for 3 months.

hb-019.explain: Warning signs are triangular with vertex at the top, white background, black icons, and red frame.

hb-020.text: What does a blue circular regulatory sign indicate?
hb-020.explain: Blue circular signs indicate a mandatory obligation (e.g. minimum speed, compulsory direction).

hb-021.text: What color are temporary work area signs?
hb-021.explain: Temporary work area signs are yellow with a red frame.

hb-022.text: What color background indicates a guide sign to cities and villages outside city limits?
hb-022.explain: Blue background with white letters indicates guide signs outside city limits, referring to cities and villages.

hb-023.text: What is the minimum distance to maintain behind an emergency vehicle?
hb-023.explain: It is prohibited to drive directly behind emergency vehicles. A distance of at least 50 meters must be maintained.

hb-024.text: What must all other vehicles do when a school bus stops to let students in or out?
hb-024.explain: All vehicles must stop and overtaking a stopped school bus is prohibited.

hb-025.text: At what age may children NOT sit in the front seat?
hb-025.explain: Children under 10 must not be in the front seat unless the rear seats are unavailable (with child-friendly seat).

hb-026.text: Who must wear a seat belt?
hb-026.explain: The driver and all other passengers must use a seat belt while driving on the roads.

hb-027.text: What does the abbreviation MSSSM stand for when changing lanes?
hb-027.explain: MSSSM: Mirrors -> Signal -> Shoulder (blind spot check) -> Speed -> Move.

hb-028.text: What is the maximum permitted reversing distance on a public road?
hb-028.explain: Not permissible to drive backwards for more than 20 meters. Prohibited entirely on highways.

hb-029.text: What should you do when the traffic light turns yellow/orange?
hb-029.a: Accelerate to cross the intersection quickly
hb-029.b: Stop if possible without endangering yourself or others
hb-029.explain: When the light turns yellow/orange, stop if it is possible to do so safely; do not cross the stop line.

hb-030.text: What is the required speed when turning right on a red light?
hb-030.explain: When turning right at a red light, your speed must be less than 15 km/h and you must stop completely for 2-3 seconds first.

hb-031.text: At an uncontrolled equal intersection, two cars arrive at the same time. Which has priority?
hb-031.explain: The right-before-left rule: if two vehicles arrive simultaneously, the vehicle on the right has right-of-way.

hb-032.text: Who has priority between a vehicle on the highway and one entering from a secondary road?
hb-032.a: The vehicle on the secondary road
hb-032.explain: The driver on the highway always has the right of way over the driver coming from a secondary road.

hb-033.text: Who has priority at a roundabout?
hb-033.b: The vehicle already inside the roundabout
hb-033.explain: Drivers approaching a roundabout must give way to vehicles already traveling inside the roundabout.

hb-034.text: What is prohibited at railway crossings?
hb-034.explain: It is prohibited to stop on rails, park on railways, or drive along the rails.

hb-035.text: What is the maximum speed for large vehicles within city roads?
hb-035.explain: Drivers of large vehicles must not exceed 50 km/h on city roads within cities.

hb-036.text: What is the minimum following distance (two-second rule)?
hb-036.explain: The minimum distance to drive behind another vehicle is two seconds (the two-second rule).

hb-037.text: What speed range is considered optimal for fuel saving?
hb-037.explain: Speed between 70 to 90 km/h saves fuel. Avoid driving at any speed exceeding 100 km/h when trying to save fuel.

hb-038.text: On which side must you normally overtake another vehicle?
hb-038.explain: Vehicles must normally be overtaken on the left side of the road.

hb-039.text: Overtaking is prohibited on which of the following?
hb-039.explain: Overtaking is prohibited at pedestrian crossings, intersections, railway lanes, bridges, curves, slippery roads, etc.

hb-040.text: When are high beams prohibited within city limits?
hb-040.explain: Within city limits, drivers must always use regular low beam lights. High beams are always prohibited in cities.

hb-041.text: What is the minimum distance you must park from a fire hydrant?
hb-041.explain: It is forbidden to stop the vehicle within 7 meters of a fire hydrant.

hb-042.text: What is the minimum distance to park from a traffic light?
hb-042.explain: It is forbidden to stop the vehicle at a distance of less than 15 meters from a traffic light.

hb-043.text: What is the minimum distance to park from a tunnel or bridge?
hb-043.explain: It is prohibited to park within 20 meters of tunnels or bridges, or on bridges themselves.

hb-044.text: What does a RED dashboard warning light mean?
hb-044.c: Stop immediately and consult vehicle manual
hb-044.explain: A red dashboard warning light means stop immediately and consult the vehicle manual.

hb-045.text: When should you fill the fuel tank according to the handbook?
hb-045.a: When the fuel indicator is at half
hb-045.b: When the fuel indicator is at a quarter
hb-045.c: When the low fuel warning light comes on
hb-045.d: When the tank is completely empty
hb-045.explain: You must fill the fuel tank when the indicator is at a quarter of the tank to avoid running out on the road.

hb-046.text: A traffic officer tells you to stop at a green light. What should you do?
hb-046.a: Proceed because the light is green
hb-046.c: Stop and follow the officer's instructions
hb-046.d: Flash headlights to warn the officer
hb-046.explain: Traffic officer instructions take priority over all traffic regulations including traffic lights.

hb-047.text: What must a driver do if their vehicle breaks down on the road?
hb-047.a: Leave the vehicle and wait on the sidewalk
hb-047.b: Clear the road immediately; place warning signs (day) or red lights (night)
hb-047.c: Call for help and stay in the vehicle
hb-047.d: Leave the vehicle running with hazard lights on
hb-047.explain: If the vehicle breaks down, clear the road immediately and drive to a side street.

hb-048.text: How long must you stop at a STOP sign?
hb-048.explain: Stop completely for 3 seconds to keep an eye on traffic or other road users from all directions.

hb-049.text: What does a double continuous line between two lanes mean?
hb-049.c: You are prohibited from crossing to the other lane
hb-049.explain: A double continuous line means drivers are prohibited from crossing this line to the other lane.

hb-050.text: At what speed range is drifting typically performed?
hb-050.explain: Drifting is a form of racing in which vehicles are driven at extremely high speeds of about 160 to 260 km/h on wide highways.

trafficFines.title: Traffic Fines in Saudi Arabia (Educational Guide)
trafficFines.subtitle: All fine tables from the official Saudi driving handbook
trafficFines.paymentDesc: Pay the minimum fine within 30 days at the nearest specialized center. After 30 days, the maximum fine applies.
trafficFines.intro: Saudi Arabia applies traffic fines to encourage safer driving and reduce accidents. Violations are grouped by how serious they are, and each group generally carries a financial penalty. More serious or repeated violations can lead to higher fines and additional penalties.

categories.minor: Minor violations: Lower fines, usually for parking issues or minor non-compliance.
categories.moderate: Moderate violations: Medium fines for behaviors such as not wearing a seatbelt or light speeding.
categories.serious: Serious violations: Higher fines for dangerous behavior such as using a mobile phone while driving, running red lights, or excessive speeding.
categories.verySerious: Very serious violations: Heavy fines and additional penalties for actions that endanger lives.

trafficFines.closing: Drivers are encouraged to follow traffic rules to avoid fines and contribute to safer roads.
trafficFines.driftingDesc: Drifting (160–260 km/h) is extremely dangerous and illegal

about.title: About
about.description1: Saudi Driving Theory Test is an educational app designed to help learners practice and prepare for the Saudi driving license theory exam through mock questions and self-assessment tests.
about.description2: The app focuses on general traffic rules, road signs, and driving safety concepts commonly included in the theory test syllabus.
about.feature1: Practice questions for driving theory preparation
about.disclaimerBody: This app is an independent educational and practice tool. It is NOT affiliated with, endorsed by, or officially connected to any government entity. For official and up-to-date information, users should always refer to the official Saudi government websites listed above.
